resources.string: Taps the screen at the points you place with Macro Maker\'s floating controls. It cannot read what is on your screen, and the app has no internet access.
Taps the screen for you — at the spots you choose, as often as you set. Free, no ads, no internet.

Macro Maker needs Android's Accessibility permission. It uses it for one thing only: tapping the screen at the points you place. It cannot read what is on your screen, and the app has no internet access, so nothing ever leaves your phone.

Next, Android opens its Accessibility settings: tap "Macro Maker taps", switch it on, and press Allow. Android shows the same "full control" warning for every app that uses this permission — Macro Maker is set up to tap only.

If Android says "Restricted setting": open Settings → Apps → Macro Maker → ⋮ (top right) → Allow restricted settings, then try again.
Stop after this many taps (0 = never)
Stop after this many seconds (0 = never)

1. Press + on the floating panel. A numbered circle appears.
2. Drag the circle onto the spot you want tapped. Add more circles to tap several spots in order.
3. Press ▶ to start and ■ to stop. ✕ stops and hides the panel; bring it back with "Show the floating controls" here.
4. Drag ✥ to move the panel out of the way.
Auto-tapping can break a game\'s rules. Use it where it\'s allowed.
Add a tap point with + first
Android refused the tap. Switch Macro Maker off and on again in Accessibility settings.
